https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/new.text: As an accordion plays, 80-year-old Maime Kapten spins across a grassy field, her embroidered skirt swirling around her as the silver chains and coins around her neck jangle with every step.For one day each year, the quiet village of Mikitamäe in southeastern Estonia transforms into something that does not exist on any map: a kingdom.There are entry visas instead of tickets, a mock currency, a military parade and an elected community leader who serves as the representative of the mythical King Peko, a fertility god rooted in Seto folklore.The kingdom is fictional. The culture behind it is not.Also Read: Barbie is 'dead'? Greta Gerwig, Margot Robbie and Warner Bros. in bizarre money fight over the $1.4 billion Hollywood sensation's futureThe annual celebration is the most visible expression of the Seto people, a small ethnic community whose traditional homeland straddles the border between Estonia and Russia. The Setos have lived in the region for centuries, maintaining their own traditions, songs, costumes and language.Kapten is one of only a few thousand people who speak Seto fluently in everyday life.“This is an important cultural day for us,” Kapten said, as cited by AP. “We get to meet people we know, we get to talk, exchange a few words, give each other a hug.”The kingdom day was created in 1994, after the collapse of the Soviet Union left the Seto homeland divided by an international border. The event was designed to celebrate the community's distinct identity, preserve its language and bring together Setos scattered on either side of the border.The division has had a lasting effect.Many Setos who lived on the Russian side eventually abandoned or sold their homes and moved to Estonia. Fewer than 200 remained there. Those living on opposite sides could no longer move around the region as freely as they once had and needed visas to visit relatives and family graves.Today, Setos live across Estonia, while the Setomaa parish in their traditional homeland has fewer than 3,000 residents.Also Read: Selena Gomez accused of fraud, sued by investors over collapse of mental health startup 'Wondermind'According to Estonia's 2021 census, about 25,000 people said they could speak Seto. But linguists estimate that only a few thousand use the language in everyday life.That makes gatherings such as the annual kingdom day more than a celebration. They are also an effort to keep a culture alive.A kingdom for a people without oneMikitamäe is usually a quiet village. On Saturday, however, its streets filled with people wearing brightly colored Seto folk costumes.A local saying holds that you hear a Seto woman before you see her, thanks to the sound of the silver chains and dangling coins that adorn traditional clothing.The clothes themselves carry information about the wearer, according to cultural activist Piret Torm-Kriis, 62. A century ago, such clothing was worn every day; today it is generally reserved for special occasions.“Seto clothes say a lot about the person who wears them,” Torm-Kriis said, as reported by AP. “If you look at a Seto woman, you can understand whether she is married or single, whether she is going to the church or to the market, to a party or to work.”Seto culture blends Eastern Orthodox Christianity with older pre-Christian beliefs.Also Read: The female breadwinner era is here: Why millions more women are working while younger men are quietly leaving the labor forceSetos attended church while also turning to Peko, a figure in local folklore associated with fertility and regarded as the king of the Setos. The connection survives through the annual election of an Ülemsootska, the community's representative and Peko's messenger.The election is theatrical but serious.Candidates — a man and a woman — present their programs to the community while standing on tree stumps. Supporters then line up behind their preferred candidate, holding onto threads that can stretch for hundreds of meters.This year's longest line formed behind folk costume maker Ingrit Kala, who was declared the new Ülemsootska.Her priorities include promoting Seto culture and ensuring the survival of the Seto language.“We have so many different things, so many skilled craftspeople, to show what a rich culture we have and to really introduce it,” Kala told AP.A language carried through songOne of the defining features of Seto culture is leelo, a distinctive form of traditional singing believed to be more than 1,000 years old and recognized by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.A woman typically begins by singing the first line. A choir joins in on the final syllables, creating a layered sound as the voices merge.The songs, whose themes often draw on mythology, were traditionally passed from one generation to another by word of mouth. They once accompanied almost every aspect of daily life, from work and rituals to celebrations.Leelo is also a record of a world that has largely disappeared.Also Read: What happened inside Indiana Tim Hortons? 75-year-old customer dies after fight but employee escapes criminal chargesThe songs contain clues about how earlier generations understood their surroundings and what they valued, said Mari Palolill, a leelo researcher and teacher, after performing with her choir.It tells us, she said to AP, “How were they thinking, what was important, what did they believe in.”That oral tradition remains central to the survival of Seto.There is now a Seto-speaking kindergarten group in Setomaa, as well as a newspaper published in the language. Several books have also been translated into Seto, including Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's “The Little Prince.”But the language remains largely a family language, Kala added.“If Seto isn’t spoken at home, then what children learn at school doesn’t help much,” she said.For younger Setos, the challenge is not simply to preserve an inheritance but to make it feel relevant.Maria Grünberg, 23, learned Seto by listening to leelo songs as a child and attempting to sing along. She now leads a youth leelo choir.Wearing a traditional Seto dress that she customized herself, along with jewelry belonging to her grandparents, Grünberg said she wants younger generations to see the culture as something they can claim as their own.“We all together try to preserve the songs, the language, and show also other young people that Seto songs and Seto language is not only for old people,” Grünberg said, as cited by AP. “We want to show that this is for everyone.”For a community whose homeland was split by a border and whose language is spoken by only a small number of people in daily life, the one-day kingdom offers an unusual kind of continuity.The kingdom may have its own ruler, currency and army, but its real purpose is simpler: to give the Seto people a place, at least for a day, where their culture is at the center of everything.

https://www.koreaherald.com/article/1085.text: South Korea launches first container ship pilot voyage through Northeast Passage Published : Aug. 24, 2026 - 16:06:03 Add The Korea Herald on Google Link copied! Shin Yong-bae Lee Soo-ho, director general of the Arctic Route Promotion Headquarters at the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, speaks in a press meeting in Busan on Thursday. (Oceans Ministry) BUSAN — South Korea will launch its first pilot operation of a container ship through the Northeast Passage on Saturday, as the government steps up efforts to develop new Arctic shipping routes and assess their commercial potential. The Panstar Acro, 2,758 twenty-foot equivalent units in size, operated by Panstar Line.com Co., will depart from Busan New Port for a 45-day round trip to Europe via the Arctic route. The vessel will sail through the Northeast Passage and call at Felixstowe in England, Rotterdam in the Netherlands and Gdansk in Poland, before returning to Busan. The voyage is part of the government’s initiative to secure new trade routes through Arctic shipping. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries has been preparing the operation with the public-private council for the revitalization of the Arctic route, launched in January. The Korea Maritime Promotion Corp. and Korea Shipping Association selected Panstar Line.com as the operator through a public bidding process in May. Since then, the ministry and related organizations have worked with the company to secure the vessel and cargo, prepare the crew, arrange insurance and establish emergency response procedures. This infographic illustrates the Northern Sea Route — a strategic shipping lane across the Arctic Ocean that connects Europe to Asia by passing along the northern coast of Russia. (Oceans Ministry) The Panstar Acro is expected to enter the Arctic Ocean around Aug. 30 and complete its Arctic crossing by approximately Sept. 7. The Arctic section of the voyage is expected to cover about 6,400 kilometers and take roughly eight days on the Europe-bound route. The vessel is scheduled to arrive at Felixstowe around Sept. 9, Rotterdam around Sept. 11 and Gdansk around Sept. 15. It is expected to return to Busan New Port around Oct. 5, although the route and schedule may change depending on weather and other conditions. The ship will carry 837 TEUs of cargo, including about 737 TEUs of commercial goods such as chemical products, used vehicles and auto parts, along with 100 empty containers. The ministry will use the voyage to evaluate the route’s technical, environmental and commercial feasibility, as well as demand from shippers and logistics companies. The voyage marks South Korea’s first container ship pilot operation through the Northeast Passage and the resumption of commercial operations on the route by a Korean shipping company for the first time since 2016. The ministry plans to analyze the route’s sailing distance, travel time, fuel consumption and operating costs. It is also pursuing cooperation on the Northwest Passage. On Aug. 5, the Ulsan Port Authority and Korea Maritime Promotion Corp. signed a memorandum of understanding with a Dutch shipping company experienced in polar navigation to share information and operational expertise and explore potential cargo demand for the Northwest Passage. Lee Soo-ho, director general of the Arctic Route Promotion Headquarters at the ministry, said the pilot voyage would serve as the first practical test of the Northeast Passage using an actual vessel and commercial cargo. “We will prioritize safety and compliance with international standards and manage the operation meticulously until the very end,” Lee said, adding that the government would continue preparing for Arctic shipping opportunities involving Korea’s shipping, shipbuilding, port and logistics industries. shinyb@heraldcorp.com Shin Yong-bae South Korea’s Oceans Ministry unveils record 2027 budget to drive maritime growth South Korea proposes record W22.2 trillion agriculture budget for 2027 K-meat gains ground in Singapore as hanwoo, handon exports expand good 0 sad 0 angry 0 recommended 0 More from Headlines Lee arrives in France, set for summit with Macron in Paris South Korean President Lee Jae Myung arrived in Nice, France, on Sunday on a four-day visit that will later take him to Paris for a bilateral summit with French President Emmanuel Macron. https://24.hu/elet-stilus/2026/11/10/meg.text: Meghan Markle kedden először jelent meg a nyilvánosság előtt azóta, hogy apját, Thomas Markle-t gyermekek szexuális bántalmazását ábrázoló felvételek birtoklásával vádolták meg az Egyesült Államokban. A sussexi hercegné férjével, Harry herceggel vett részt egy brüsszeli rendezvényen, ám a sajtó kérdéseire nem válaszolt – írja a Page Six. A házaspár az Európai Parlamentben nyitotta meg a Lost Screen Memorial című installációt. Az emlékhely azoknak a gyerekeknek állít emléket, akiknek halála a közösségi média káros hatásaival hozható összefüggésbe. A feketébe öltözött Markle az eseményen végig férje kezét fogta, és eredetileg beszédet is mondott volna, ám végül visszalépett a felszólalástól. A Page Six értesülése szerint úgy érezte, a családját érintő történtek után nincs elég lelkiereje a nyilvános megszólaláshoz. A herceg ugyanakkor beszédet mondott a rendezvényen. A gyermekek online biztonságának fontosságát hangsúlyozta, és arra szólította fel a döntéshozókat, hogy szigorúbban lépjenek fel a közösségimédia-platformokkal szemben. A 82 éves Thomas Markle-t november 6-án tartóztatták le, Floridában. Az amerikai hatóságok szerint a férfi közel húsz éven át bérelt két raktárhelyiséget Los Angeles környékén. Az FBI ezek átkutatása során 78 tárgyat foglalt le , köztük fényképeket, filmnegatívokat és könyveket. A nyomozók szerint a lefoglalt anyagok között gyermekek szexuális bántalmazását ábrázoló felvételek is voltak. A vádirat szerint egyes képeken maga Markle is szerepelhet, kiskorú lányokkal. A férfi korábban tagadta az ellene felhozott vádakat . Markle-t a bíróság elektronikus nyomkövetővel és házi őrizettel engedte szabadon. Egy floridai bíró pszichiátriai vizsgálatot is elrendelt, annak megállapítására, hogy a férfi képes-e részt venni a büntetőeljárásban. Bűnössége esetén akár húsz év börtönbüntetésre is ítélhetik. Meghan Markle korábban közleményben reagált az apjával kapcsolatos vádakra. Mint fogalmazott, mélyen megrendítették a történtek, és reméli, hogy az igazságszolgáltatás megfelelően jár el az ügyben. A hercegné azt is elmondta, hogy már 2018-ban tudomást szerzett az apját érintő, aggasztó állításokról. Állítása szerint ezért döntött úgy, hogy megszakítja vele a kapcsolatot, és nem engedi, hogy találkozzon a gyermekeivel.
